6) Attached terms. Exhibit A forms part of this agreement. Resolve blank information and attach required disclosures and addenda before a live signing request.

7) Assigned contract interest. Assignor assigns to Assignee its purchaser interest in the executed purchase agreement for the property in Deal Terms, subject to that agreement, all amendments, required disclosures, assignment consents and applicable law. Attach the complete executed purchase agreement. This transfers a contractual interest, not present ownership of the property. Assignor is a principal and may receive the stated assignment fee.

8) Price, fee and closing. Assignee assumes the underlying purchase obligations and pays the underlying purchase price plus the stated assignment fee and agreed closing charges. The fee is payable through the closing agent at funding. The underlying purchase agreement controls the closing deadline; this assignment does not restart a 30-day period or extend any deadline. Any different date needs a valid amendment with the required parties.

9) Deposit and credit. Assignee deposits the stated buyer deposit with the named escrow agent within one business day after the last assignment signature unless otherwise agreed in writing. The deposit is credited toward the assignment fee at closing. Any excess allocation requires signed escrow instructions. Deposit is not confirmed received, immediately earned or payable directly to Assignor merely because this agreement is signed.

10) Non-refundable terms and exceptions. After execution, the deposit is non-refundable for Assignee default only to the extent the signed terms and applicable law permit. It remains refundable where Assignor cannot convey the stated contract interest, required consent is refused, Seller defaults, unresolved title prevents closing, or the underlying contract validly terminates without Assignee default. Mandatory cancellation and refund rights prevail. Escrow must not release disputed funds without proper authority.

11) Buyer withdrawal and default. Assignee must promptly deliver written notice of a withdrawal request and its stated basis to Assignor and escrow. Withdrawal does not itself terminate the underlying seller agreement, release Assignor, cancel escrow duties or authorize a replacement assignment. Assignment termination, release, deposit treatment and remaining liability require review under the signed documents and applicable law. No automatic second sale of the same contract interest is authorized.

12) Due diligence, access and occupancy. Assignee acknowledges receipt of the executed underlying agreement and amendments and independently evaluates condition, value, repairs and title. No new inspection right is created; transferred remaining rights must be stated expressly. Proof of funds and authority to sign may be required. Showings require Seller/occupant approval. Existing tenancy, possession and security-deposit arrangements remain governed by the underlying documents and law.

13) Costs and retained obligations. Assignee pays closing charges legally allocable to Buyer. Seller remains responsible for existing mortgages, liens, unpaid obligations and charges law requires Seller to pay unless validly agreed otherwise. Assignment does not release Assignor from the seller agreement without Seller's written consent. Taxes, prorations and fee allocations must be disclosed on the final settlement statement.

14) Entire agreement and notices. The executed purchase agreement, required disclosures, this assignment and signed addenda govern the transaction. Changes, extensions, cancellation agreements and releases require appropriate signed writings. Electronic records and signatures may be used with the signers' consent. Neither the software nor an AI conversation confirms funds, title acceptance, release of liability or a completed closing.
